metric.why: Idle servers burn power, licenses, and depreciation while producing nothing. Fleet utilization is where the money hides in most enterprise estates, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.
metric.definition: The share of provisioned compute doing real work, measured over time rather than at peak.

reading.body:
Server utilization rate is the share of provisioned compute doing real work over time, not at peak, and it is the denominator that makes every efficiency metric honest.

The metric is defined against time rather than against the busiest moment. A fleet measured at peak looks fully used by construction, because peak is the instant the denominator was chosen to flatter. Measured over time, the same fleet reveals the gap between what was provisioned and what was actually needed.

That gap is where the cost sits. Idle servers still draw power, still hold licenses, and still depreciate. For AI specifically, the provisioned compute is expensive and the power behind it is the scarce input, so utilization is the difference between capacity that produces tokens and capacity that produces a bill.

The data covers one metric and its definition, alongside two sibling measures of capacity and server use, stranded power and space per cabinet, and floor loading limits. It does not give a utilization figure, a trend, or a comparison across operators, so it establishes what to measure and why, not how any particular fleet currently performs.
